column1: # The load smokes CI's `smokes` job doesn't expect to pass today (D-209 addendum), each a known debt with its decision
# and owner. No threshold is changed for them: each still runs at check.sh's settings and prints its numbers.
# scripts/smoke-verdict.sh judges the job by this list:
#   strict    fails on every run today. A strict smoke that PASSES fails the job ("remove it from the list"); the fix
#             that makes it pass removes its own line in the same change.
#   flapping  straddles its limit on runner noise (about 2x run to run on the same code). Either outcome is allowed
#             against its normal limit, but its CEILING (2x the limit) fails the job whatever the list says, so a real
#             regression can't hide here. It leaves this list when D-209's normalised gate judges it by margin over the
#             runner's measured baseline.
# A smoke that fails and isn't listed fails the job.
# Each job judges only its own entries (SMOKE_SCOPE): the smokes job's are plain names; the integration job's load
# smokes are `integration/<endpoint>-<scenario>`. Runner speed needs no entry (D-221): each job measures its runner
# (scripts/runner-speed.sh) and scales fixed rates down, and back-to-back limits up, to it; under half the reference
# speed latency isn't judged. Hard failures (a failed check, a real request error, assets' uploads refused) are never
# tolerated, listed or not.
# Columns, tab-separated: smoke, kind, decision, owner, ceiling, measured (CI 44543394086 → 44551888337, the 4-core
# runner), what is owed. A ceiling is `p99<=MS` (the run's overall p99) or `l08<=RATIO` (L08's worst noise/baseline ratio).
# A ceiling marked `EXPIRES-WITH D-NNN` is a temporary tolerance for a known, owned defect: the verdict refuses it once
# docs/DECISIONS.md has D-NNN's row (its fix merged), and that fix removes the entry or restores the ordinary 2x ceiling.
# noisy-agent's ceiling was a temporary 8 (its measured worst, 6.56, plus about 25%) until D-214 took refused requests off
# the pool; it is back at the ordinary 4 (2x its limit).
